 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Pakistan will swap their usual green kit for a pink jersey against Sri Lanka on Sunday to mark Breast Cancer Awareness Month.
 The PCB is running the drive with Pink Ribbon Pakistan, adding pink ribbons, boundary boards, stumps and free mammogram checkups for women.
 Pakistan trained hard at Pindi Stadium under Mike Hesson, with Shaheen Shah Afridi captaining the side in a series that starts on Sunday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Why are Pakistan wearing pink kits against Sri Lanka? 
 Pakistan's players will leave their familiar green shirts in the dressing room on Sunday and walk out in pink instead when they host Sri Lanka in the opening match of the PAK vs SL vs ENG ODI tri-series at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
 The pink-themed jersey marks Breast Cancer Awareness Month, also known as #Pinktober.
 The change is part of the Pakistan Cricket Board's corporate social responsibility partnership with Pink Ribbon Pakistan. The aim is simple enough: to push more women towards early diagnosis and regular screening, since catching the disease early can improve a patient's chances of survival by a big margin.
 It won't only be the Pakistan players who show their support. Sri Lanka's players, the match officials and the coaching staff will all have pink ribbons pinned to their collars and shirts, so the whole field becomes a show of solidarity.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The ground will join in as well, with pink branding on the LED boundary boards, the match-day signage and even the stumps. Viewers at home will see the same theme, because commentators and presenters will wear pink ribbons too and share awareness and prevention figures through the live international broadcast.
 MORE: Mitchell Starc's IPL 2027 availability in doubt: Could he face a two-season ban and will Delhi Capitals release him before mini-auction? 
 Pink Day tradition and the PCB's own record
 South Africa made the pink ODI famous through its "Pink Day" match at the Wanderers in Johannesburg, which backs breast cancer clinics.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pakistan's board has built its own habit along similar lines, regularly working the cause into the Pakistan Super League and designated home fixtures in October. So Sunday's pink jersey fits a pattern and isn't a one-off gesture.
 MORE:  Pink Day in South African cricket explained: Why the Proteas wear pink jersey at Johannesburg 
 On the cricket side, Pakistan went through a tough training session at Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi on Thursday to sharpen up for the tri-series, which begins on Sunday. Sri Lanka trained as well, while England were due to land on Friday morning, according to the PCB.
 The Pakistan players worked on batting, bowling and fielding under head coach Mike Hesson, who recently guided them to a 2-1 win over Sri Lanka in the T20I series at the same venue.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The squad gathered in Islamabad on Wednesday night for what's seen as the most important assignment before next year's World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, since it helps all three teams get ready for that tournament.
 Ace pacer Shaheen Shah Afridi will lead the side, and Babar Azam, Fakhar Zaman, Salman Ali Agha, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf are also part of the series. Nine players from the recent T20I series will feature in the ODI team, and the matches will be shared between Pindi and Lahore.
